supports: deterministic Rule execution and replay integrity

dataset_limitations: The twelve frozen records are noisy secondary or tertiary extracts: two breach articles are duplicated/truncated, several contain scraper chrome, and SRC002, SRC004, SRC006 and SRC012 are tangential or temporally remote.
The May 2015 date describes the affected patient-record cohort, not a demonstrated intrusion start. The simulation does not adopt the Draft's nearly-three-year access duration as verified timing.

Whitefly attribution is retrospective and remains a published claim. The actor and capability vocabulary reveals attribution-related names before their generated publication; the package is not historically prefix-clean.

The Draft turns database ownership, data theft, security failures, public naming, investigation subject status, penalty receipt and patient notification into actor actions; these remain context or environment results unless a bounded choice is explicit.
Draft E4/E5 relation endpoints and E6 penalty descriptions are reversed or inconsistent. Actor-local rows, two penalty transactions and frozen text control the qualified authority map.
Fine payment, individual notification, patient harm, exploit mechanics, completed remediation and cybersecurity effectiveness lack executable state mechanisms and remain outside the reducer.
Full Draft exposure and authored logical-time compression preclude unbiased prediction, timing calibration, historical fit, attacker-truth or held-out claims.
